solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Data belonging to part of UK turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: of expresses possession, as in 'the house of my father'
NI is Northern Ireland, one of the four parts of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Figures relating to some region of Britain have come to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, which is facts or figures.

clue.text: Mix socially in hot spot with wealthy person

parts.note: a hob is the heated top of a cooker, a literal hot spot
a nob is British slang for a rich or upper-class person

explanation.surface: A guest mingling at a fashionable venue alongside a rich celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot spot' reads as a trendy venue, but it is the cooker hob; a nob is a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to socialise familiarly, especially with people of higher status.

clue.text: Basil, for example, in Sybil's heart?

parts.note: a pronoun for a woman's possession: hers
the heart of Sybil's name, its central letter, is B; the name does double duty, flagged by the question mark

explanation.surface: Fawlty Towers: Basil Fawlty's wife Sybil — is he truly in her heart?
explanation.walkthrough: Sybil's name works twice: it gives the pronoun HER and its own central letter B. The question mark flags that double duty; Basil and Sybil are the hotelier couple in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary plant used to flavour food, an example of the class of seasoning plants.

clue.text: Score halved, then point is added in game

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half of it is ten
a compass point, here north
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports report: one side's tally cut in half, then a point added mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'point' sound like scoring in a match, but a score is the number twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a competitive pastime played over sets and games.

clue.text: Part of wood I'm in I should cut down

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the run of letters straddles wood, I'm, in, I and should

explanation.surface: Someone lost in a forest feels they ought to fell some trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' looks like chopping trees in the wood, but it is the definition: reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to reduce or lessen, which is to cut something down in size.

clue.text: Showing how old we are in company, you and me — that's brave

indicators.note: one group of letters sits inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: our age states how old we are
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: Revealing your age among friends takes some nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous means bold and unafraid, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: Release articles in French about hostile takeover

indicators.note: the two French articles go around the takeover word

parts.note: UN and LE are the French indefinite and definite articles
a coup is the violent seizure of power

explanation.surface: A French newspaper releases stories on a hostile business takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hostile takeover' suggests the business world, but it is a political coup.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to detach or set free, as a railway carriage is released from a train.

clue.text: French scientist's gone over street there, heading North

parts.note: past means gone by, over and done

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: there points to France, the scientist's country: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A French scientist has crossed the road and is going north.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'; 'there' means in France, so the street is a French rue.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the nineteenth-century French chemist who developed pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Source of leaders some discredit, originally

indicators.note: only some of the letters across these words are taken, a run spanning both

parts.note: the run starts at the end of discredit and runs into the start of originally

explanation.surface: Where the headlines come from: some originally discredited source.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaders here are newspaper editorials, which an editor writes.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor writes or commissions the leading articles, the paper's opinion pieces.

clue.text: Establishes nothing has been deposited in financial resources

indicators.note: like money paid into an account, one letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: funds are money available to spend
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A bank statement shows no deposits have been made into the account.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, a synonym of establish.

clue.text: Criminal behaviour from musicians I hear

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
taken as written
to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: A rumour that a group of musicians has been up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' reads as hearsay, but 'hear' is the judge's verb try.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by bandits, lawless conduct by outlaws.

clue.text: Cheating in first of down clues — so boring must be changed

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of down

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumbling solver says the setter cheats: these down clues are so dull they need rewriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-cross is a betrayal of someone you pretended to help, so double-crossing is deceiving or cheating.

clue.text: European taken in by cop — driver mistreated with excessive charge

indicators.note: one letter is held within the other letters
badly handled letters, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traffic policeman takes in a European motorist and is accused of abusing him with an unfair fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excessive charge' sounds like a police charge, but it means a price that is too high.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs more than it is worth, so it carries an excessive price.

clue.text: Bishop in pub upset one other religious leader

indicators.note: the chess bishop's letter is placed inside the other word
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place

explanation.surface: A bishop gets drunk in a pub, unsettling another church leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other' is fair because a bishop leads one faith and the answer leads another.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher who leads a congregation in worship.

clue.text: Piece of reading material that's found on plane, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a page of a book
second meaning: the foliage of a tree such as the plane

explanation.walkthrough: The plane looks like an aircraft with in-flight magazines, but it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is both a single sheet of a book and a flat green part growing on a tree.

clue.text: Best at running exam — left in charge over it

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part is placed above the next
the letter for left sits inside the word for a charge

parts.note: a fee is a payment charged
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Someone excellent at running an exam leaves the person in charge to supervise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests managing the exam, but the definition is about speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift, so the fleetest runner is the fastest, best at running.

clue.text: Crazy British at centre of attack

indicators.note: placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a raid is a sudden assault

explanation.surface: A wild Briton is at the heart of the assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid literally means having rabies, and figuratively fanatical or crazed.

clue.text: Garment repeatedly found in knitting patterns

parts.note: double means twice over
the word knitting contains a pair of T letters, a double T

explanation.surface: A garment that keeps showing up in knitting designs.
explanation.walkthrough: The double letter in the word 'knitting' is the trick: it has TT, a double T.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Renaissance times.

clue.text: Catch leader of pirates

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... catches or fastens
second meaning: Captain ..., the pirate chief in Peter Pan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of pirates' looks like the first letter of a word, but it is Captain Hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a catch or fastener, and also the villainous captain in J. M. Barrie's story.

clue.text: Cherished quality about one child, initially, showing early development

indicators.note: the longer word goes around the other letters

parts.note: preciousness is the quality of being treasured

indicators.note: only the opening letters of these words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of one and child

explanation.surface: A doting parent prizes the gifts of one child who is ahead for their age.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocious describes a child who has developed abilities unusually early.

clue.text: Ring with a measure of power raised capital

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted up, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a watt is the unit of power

explanation.surface: An electrician's ring main and a unit of power, lifted up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Person from that place not knowing about end of conflict

indicators.note: the first word goes around the other letter

parts.note: naive means innocent, lacking knowledge

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of conflict

explanation.surface: A local who knows nothing about how the war ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a particular place, an inhabitant by birth.

clue.text: Orders acid test rearranged

indicators.note: the letters are put into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lab demands that the acid test be done again.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to command or lay down rules, so dictates are orders.

clue.text: Criticise what needs a lot of tricks to succeed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to attack harshly in words

definitions.text: what needs a lot of tricks to succeed
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in bridge a ... is a contract to win all or all but one of the tricks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricks' sound like a con artist's, but they are bridge tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam means to criticise severely, and in the card game bridge it is a bid to take nearly every trick.

clue.text: Latin adapted by clergy, finally, for part of service

indicators.note: altered, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of clergy

explanation.surface: Clergy rework a Latin text for use in worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of prayers with responses recited in church worship.

clue.text: Not easy without drink consumed? That's curious

indicators.note: the drink's letters are taken out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
tea is a drink, here taken away

explanation.surface: Getting through the day without a cuppa is hard; why ask?
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy means prying or inquisitive, a nosy person being curious about others' affairs.

clue.text: Set eyes on, now and then, playground equipment

parts.note: see is to set eyes on, in the present tense
now gives the present, see; then gives the past, saw

explanation.surface: A passer-by notices a playground ride from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' looks like 'occasionally', but it asks for the verb in present then past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a plank balanced in the middle for children to ride up and down.

clue.text: Militant has view restricted after start of play

indicators.note: the cut-down word comes after the start of the play

parts.note: Act I is the opening section of a play

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a vista is a view

explanation.surface: A protester's view is obstructed once the play begins.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist campaigns vigorously for a cause, which a militant does aggressively.
